pos.personaBrief: Possession is the core idea: 68-75% for Barcelona, 'they even use the ball to defend', Xavi 'the one who has the ball is master of the game', and Spain 'will not change style' against weaker sides.

pro.personaBrief: Short passing build-up with the keeper as auxiliary sweeper; Barcelona eschew the quick counter and use safe, patient circulation including sideways passes.

est.personaBrief: Rondo-based close combinations, a false 9 and midfielders playing short in tight spaces, within a structured 4-3-3 with defined roles; narrow play with players close together.

lar.personaBrief: Technical midfielders in the centre, narrow play, 4-6-0 without a striker in 2012; wingers were not the main route.

blo.personaBrief: Barcelona pressed immediately after losing the ball and high with the front three; Spain 2008 pressed less, but the model is high line and counter-press, never a deep block.

mar.personaBrief: No marking evidence in period; the 3-1 rule and spatial organisation suggest zone, and opponents man-marked Xavi rather than the reverse.

pla.personaBrief: Spain stated 'we are not going to change our style'; the style is defined and imposed built on La Masia players, kept regardless of opponent.

res.personaBrief: Style-first and committed to playing the same way for beauty and control, but built to win; no settling for draws or shutting games.

sis.personaBrief: A collective system with stars all working off the ball (work rate off the ball at Barcelona), roles defined for everyone.

jog.personaBrief: Technical midfielders like Xavi and Iniesta, rondos and 'receive, pass, offer'; technique over pace and power.

bas.personaBrief: La Masia core: 10 of 14 Barcelona players and six of Spain's 2010 players came from the academy; Aragones favoured younger strikers.

lid.personaBrief: Aragones and Guardiola were demanding but personal, listening to leaders like Xavi and keeping a united group; the rules applied to all.
